recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-43484 unless FHIR-I later makes a broader decision to add rationale about computable definitional artifacts across ExampleScenario or related resources.
issue_request: FHIR-43484 was an Applied/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-I R6 clarification asking whether ExampleScenario should be treated as a FHIR resource for data exchange. The accepted resolution replaced the older implementation-guide/specification wording with language comparing ExampleScenario to ImplementationGuide, Requirements, ActorDefinition, and similar definitional resources typically exchanged in implementation guide packages.
initial_application: Jira cites Git master 6d21a4c1c0. Commit 6d21a4c1c014f8b726b9f21861b2ce666dfc6282 changed source/examplescenario/examplescenario-introduction.xml by replacing the old opening sentence with the approved scope wording and separating the following usage sentence into a new paragraph.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively registers ExampleScenario, assigns it to fhir, and lists it as normative and approved, so the narrative file is build-scoped. FHIR-I minutes for 2024-01-08 record FHIR-43484 as P w/ mod. A later FMG resource-maturity thread lists ExampleScenario among resources recommended to stay in the main specification, and focused Jira/Zulip searches did not find a later conflicting decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. The current source already conveys the required distinction between implementation-guide package exchange for implementer understanding and clinical-system information exchange; adding the Jira rationale about computable representations would be redundant rather than necessary for implementer understanding.
